Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • As All comments: the panel on the right that lists every thread on the page, including ones in hidden views and ones whose content is gone, with the words each is about.
  • Once per page, opened from the comment control's menu or by clicking the control in comment mode.

When not to use

  • For the threads beside the content: they are cards in the column, not a panel.
  • For a thread on its own: open it where it is.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. To add variants, replace this line with one bullet per variant, each a variant id, a dash and what it is for.

Anatomy

Built from:

  • cmp-chip, variant filter — the two filters on the top line: @ For you and ✓ Resolved, each on or off.
  • cmp-icon-button, variant quiet — the close button at the end of the top line (x).
  • cmp-comment-card — one per thread, at rest or open (the open variant opens out in place); each card is preceded by the words it is about.
  • cmp-avatar, variant sm, cmp-kbd and cmp-switch — the footer: your avatar and name, Comment with its shortcut and its switch (comment mode), and ⋯ for the rest of the menu (a quiet icon button).

Own parts:

  • Root: <aside class="ds-comments-panel" aria-label="All comments">, a sheet of paper with an ink edge down its start side, the full height of the window beside the page, which moves over to make room.
  • ds-comments-panel__top: the top line: the filters at the start, the close button at the end. It has no title.
  • ds-comments-panel__list: the list of threads, <ul> with aria-label="Comments", one <li> per thread, scrolling on its own.
  • ds-comments-panel__group (with-groups): on a deck, a heading row before each slide's threads, "Slide 3 · 2 open", with this slide's group marked aria-current="true".
  • ds-comments-panel__about: before each card, the words the thread is about, or where it is when its content is gone, in the typewriter face, one line.
  • ds-comments-panel__empty: the one line shown when a filter leaves nothing ("No comments mention you").
  • ds-comments-panel__footer: the footer that the comment control turns into while the panel is open.

Accessibility

  • The panel is a complementary landmark named All comments; from the keyboard its filters and close button come first, then its cards, then its footer.
  • Screen readers hear the list as a list of comments under a heading; each filter says its word and whether it is on.
  • Esc closes the panel (after any open thread), and focus returns to the comment control.
  • Choosing a card opens it out in place and reveals where the thread is on the page; a thread with no place says where it was.

Interaction

  • Opening slides the panel in from the right edge over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease while the page eases into the narrower space; closing reverses both (int-04). The control's footer shape and its corner shape ease into each other.
  • A filter turns on and off with a colour change over --ds-motion-quick; the list's cards fade in and out as the filter changes over --ds-motion-settle.
  • Choosing a card opens it out in place; the open thread on the page, if any, moves into the panel. One thread is open at a time; choosing the open card's top line, or Esc, closes it.
  • Resolve on a card eases it out of the list over --ds-motion-settle, unless ✓ Resolved is on; then it stays, muted, with Reopen.
  • Hovering a closed card shows its actions, as any card does; the card neither moves nor changes size.
  • Under reduced motion the panel and its cards appear in place (int-06).

Content rules

  • The filters read "For you" and "Resolved", with their icons; the empty line reads "No comments mention you" or "No resolved comments".
  • The about line is the quoted words, up to one line, or "Pin · under The path", or "Content gone · was in The river".
  • The footer reads your name, "Comment" with its shortcut, and nothing else.

Do and don't

  • Do keep the panel the same width whatever it holds, and let its list scroll; on a narrow screen it takes the full width and the page waits beneath it.
  • Don't open anything on the page while the panel is open; everything happens in the panel.
  • Don't wrap anything in the top line or the footer onto a second line.
